Defaults are a 1.0 m nominal tile, 0.0007 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Building a sampler sorts 4096 pixel values (millisecond scale); prefer 512 or larger so each pixel spans at least 8 px and the weave shows, 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`radarscope` adds radar-scope display schematics, bringing the current catalog from 901 to 902 kinds (903 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one circular scope (radius 0.46 UV) on a dark green-black ground: 5 evenly spaced range rings (the outer one heavier), 24 bearing spokes every 15° (every 6th a heavier crosshair), one bright sweep arm at a seed-chosen angle, a 1.3 rad phosphor afterglow behind it that fades quadratically, and 6 blips at random polar positions (brighter the closer they are behind the arm, keeping at least 40% brightness). 192 horizontal scanlines modulate brightness, with slight noise. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored UI-style schematic: it is not the screen of any radar model and has no text, scale numbers or real range/bearing meaning; the sweep arm is fixed in the tile and does not move over time. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.0004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Each pixel loops over at most 6 blips; prefer 512 or larger to resolve the thin lines and blips, 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`hazardstripes` adds worn hazard-warning-stripe schematics, bringing the current catalog from 902 to 903 kinds (904 gallery choices including plain). Yellow-and-black stripes run at 45° (the integer shear a = u + v, 8 stripes per tile, i.e. 4 yellow and 4 black) over steel; the paint chips away according to three wear terms: 96² noise chips, scratches stretched along the stripes (192×10-cell noise in the integer-shear coordinates a = u + v and b = u − v) and an edge weight favoring stripe borders (+0.35 within 0.3 of a stripe width of a border). Where the paint is gone, bare steel shows through as the neutral gray (153,153,139) of the existing mortar mix, while the metallic M mask and the mortar weight are the same wear value (M1 = bare steel, M0 = paint). Paint keeps pure yellow / pure black base tones; roughness is 0.45 yellow, 0.62 black and 0.36 steel; paint stands 0.14 above the steel and chipped edges have slightly darker AO.

This is an authored schematic: it is not the color or stripe proportion mandated by any standard (for example OSHA or ISO 3864) and has no rust, welds, rivets or dents; bare steel is only approximated by the existing neutral gray, not an alloy or optical measurement. No external artwork is cited or shipped. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.0032 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 1; explicit `createMaterial({ metallic: 0 })` changes only the scalar factor, not the stored M mask. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger to resolve chips and scratches; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`kiwislices` adds kiwi-fruit slice schematics, bringing the current catalog from 903 to 904 kinds (905 gallery choices including plain). Each of the 2×2 cells holds one round slice (radius 0.42 of a cell, with jittered position, 92–100% scale and starting angle): green flesh with 64 pale radial fibers (darker away from the core), a pale yellow-green core disc (radius 0.115 of a cell), two rings of dark oval seeds outside the core (20 on the inner ring at 0.175 of a cell, 28 on the outer ring at 0.24, offset by half a pitch), and a dark-brown skin ring with fine fuzz noise (width 0.045 of a cell); dark gaps separate the fruit. Seeds are recessed with darker AO and the core is slightly lower; flesh is smooth (roughness 0.24) and skin rough (0.9). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic, not a measurement of any cultivar or cut: seed counts and positions, fiber count and colors are simplified, and no external artwork is cited or shipped. Each slice's radius plus its position jitter stays below half a cell, so a point only queries its own cell. Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile, 0.0018 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `mandalaflower` adds mandala-flower schematics, bringing the current catalog from 904 to 905 kinds (906 gallery choices including plain). One flower is centered on the tile center (the seed chooses its overall rotation). From the outside in: 12 large lotus petals (polar rose edge ρ = 0.30 + 0.15·|cos(6θ)|^0.8), a ring of 36 dots (radius 0.27), 24 outer petals (ρ = 0.12 + 0.11·|cos(12θ)|^1.5), 12 inner petals (phase-shifted by half a petal pitch) and a central hub (radius 0.035). Every layer is a filled region with a dark outline (width 0.008) painted back to front; the ground is recessed and later layers are higher. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored simplified schematic, not a mandala pattern of any religion, tradition or culture; no external artwork is cited or shipped. The outline width is the radial difference between the fill boundary ρ and boundary − width, not a distance perpendicular to the boundary. Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.0014 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Each pixel needs two trigonometric calls (atan2 and the rose-edge cosines); prefer 512 or larger to resolve the inner petals and the dot ring, 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`needlepoint` adds needlepoint-tapestry schematics, bringing the current catalog from 905 to 906 kinds (907 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 48×48 half-cross stitches slanted along (1, 1) (half-width 0.27 and half-length 0.66 of a cell, tapering at the ends with a fourth-power profile, plus a two-ply twist light/dark ripple), with dark canvas gaps showing between stitches. Color comes from a 12×12-stitch motif repeated 4×4 per tile: concentric diamond rings (ring width 2 stitches, a three-tone cycle) with a bright cross accent through the motif center, and every stitch has ±0.03 tone jitter. The motif is mirror-symmetric in both x and y. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored simplified schematic: it is not a measurement of a particular stitch (such as continental or basketweave) or design, and wool fuzz, canvas weave detail and the back of the work are not modeled. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.0026 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `dicefaces` adds dice-face schematics, bringing the current catalog from 906 to 907 kinds (908 gallery choices including plain). A 4×4 field of rounded-square ivory faces (half edge 0.43 of a cell, corner radius 0.11, with a domed bevel at the face edge and dark gaps between faces), each hash-chosen to carry 1–6 recessed pips. The pips sit on a 3×3 lattice (spacing 0.255 of a cell, radius 0.078) in the standard point-symmetric layouts: 1 = center; 2 = diagonal; 3 = diagonal plus center; 4 = corners; 5 = corners plus center; 6 = two rows of three; each face is also randomly turned by 90° and mirrored so the 2, 3 and 6 layouts vary in direction. Pips are hemispherical recesses (depth 0.35, darker AO); faces are glossy (roughness 0.3) and gaps rough (0.9). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic, not the specification of any dice maker: opposite faces summing to 7 and left- or right-handed numbering belong to a whole die, not a single-face texture, and are not modeled. No external artwork is cited or shipped. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.0034 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. `cinderblockwall` adds a concrete-masonry-unit wall, bringing the current catalog from 907 to 908 kinds (909 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 8 courses × 4 blocks in a half-block running bond (odd courses shifted right), blocks at a 2:1 aspect; recessed mortar joints 0.0095 tile wide use the existing `mortar` channel with the neutral grout color. Block faces carry a ±0.08 per-block tone shift, a low-frequency cloudy mottle, 160×160 aggregate grain relief, chamfered edges and about 940 small air voids per tile (one per 56×56 cell with probability 0.3, radius 0.0025–0.0059 tile) that are recessed and darker in color and AO. Metallic is 0.

This is an authored schematic, not a measurement of a particular CMU specification (such as ASTM C90 dimensions, cores and face shells): hollow cores, squeezed-out mortar, efflorescence and paint are not modeled. `moirefringes` adds moire fringes, bringing the current catalog from 908 to 909 kinds (910 gallery choices including plain). Two transparent fine-line gratings are overlaid: integer wave vectors (24, 3) and (24, −3) (24 near-vertical lines per tile with opposite small tilts), a line fraction of 0.26, and light passes only where neither sheet has ink. The gratings' difference (0, 6) forms 6 horizontal moire bands per tile (wide and light where lines coincide, dense and dark where they interleave), and their sum (48, 0) is a second, finer set of fringes; the paper also carries a low-amplitude 256×256 fiber variation in color and height. Ink lines are slightly raised and smoother; metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored optical schematic, not a physical moire simulation: there is no observer view, camera sampling or screen sub-pixels; the fringes are the mathematical product of the two gratings. Because the wave vectors are integers, both gratings and their difference and sum are continuous across the tile boundary. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.0014 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger so each line spans roughly 5 px or more; at very low resolutions or strong minification the texture itself produces extra aliasing moire. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`azulejotiles` adds Portuguese-style painted ceramic tiles, bringing the current catalog from 909 to 910 kinds (911 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds a 4×4 grid of identical glazed square tiles separated by recessed grout lines 0.012 tile wide (using the existing `mortar` channel with the neutral grout color); each tile carries a cobalt-on-white glaze design with full square symmetry: a four-lobed central rosette (radius 0.15 of a tile, lobe amplitude 0.055), a thin ring at radius 0.3, and quarter-disc corner motifs that join into full circles where four tiles meet (with a white thin ring inside). The blue has brush-stroke tone variation, the glaze carries faint craquelure lines on a 28×28 cell scale per tile, tile edges are bevelled, the glaze is smooth (roughness 0.2) and the grout rough. Metallic is 0.

This is an authored schematic, not a measurement of a particular historical design or origin (such as Delft or Talavera); there is no hand-painted variation between tiles — every tile is identical, and because the design has full square symmetry, turning a tile would make no visible difference in this material. `tumblingblocks` adds a tumbling-blocks (isometric cube) patchwork, bringing the current catalog from 910 to 911 kinds (912 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds a hexagonal lattice of 7 columns × 8 rows; every pointy-top hexagon (circumradius 1) is split by three rays from its center to the upper-right, upper-left and bottom vertices into a top face (light, tone 0.92), a right face (mid, 0.62) and a left face (dark, 0.3), giving the isometric-cube illusion. Each face also gets ±0.06 per-block tone jitter, fine woven-fabric grain, and thin seams between faces (dark, slightly recessed, darker AO). The lattice is aligned with a hexagon center at u = v = 0; because the UV tile is square and the lattice is 7√3 wide by 12 tall (about 1.01), the hexagons are stretched about 1% non-uniformly. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored patchwork schematic, not a measurement of a particular quilt design: there is no stitching, batting or fabric wrinkling, and the cubes' 3D appearance is baked tone (the light and dark faces do not respond to light direction). Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.0018 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `kilimflatweave` adds a kilim flatweave rug, bringing the current catalog from 911 to 912 kinds (913 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 48×48 weave cells arranged top to bottom in four 12-row bands: stepped diamonds (12-cell period, mirror-symmetric in both axes, stepped concentric colors), a stepped zigzag (6-cell period, each row half in each of two colors), horizontal stripes (a 12-row palindrome: dark, dark, red, red, ochre, white, white, ochre, red, red, dark, dark) and crosses (44 of the 144 cells in each 12×12 motif carry the cross color). Colors are four tone steps (indigo, madder red, saffron, undyed-wool white) with ±0.025 per-cell dye jitter, horizontal weft-faced ribs (3 per cell) and a low-amplitude fibre mottle; where the color changes between neighboring cells the cell's left edge carries a 0.14-cell-wide slit (dark, recessed, darker AO), imitating the vertical slits of a flatweave at color boundaries. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored simplified schematic, not a measurement of a particular tribe or region's kilim, and no traditional provenance is claimed; warp/weft interlacing detail, fringes and wear are not modeled. The four tone steps are brightness rather than hue (colors interpolate linearly between the dark and light ends). `ean13barcodes` adds EAN-13 barcode labels, bringing the current catalog from 912 to 913 kinds (914 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 4 labels stacked vertically, each filling the tile width (9 modules of quiet zone on each side plus 95 modules of bars, 113 modules in all), encoded per the EAN-13 specification: start guard 101, six left digits (L or G codes chosen by the first digit's parity pattern), center guard 01010, six right digits (R codes), end guard 101, and a correct thirteenth check digit. The twelve data digits derive from the seed and row (so rows differ); they are not registered product numbers and no human-readable digits are drawn. Guard bars run slightly lower than digit bars, bar edges are softened, the ink has low-amplitude density variation and the paper faint fibers. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the symbols are generated from the published EAN-13 encoding tables so that structural "scanning" is valid, but print quality (such as ISO 15416 grades), bar-width gain compensation, human-readable text and the leading digit are not modeled; the tests verify structure and check digits only and no physical scanner or decoder library was used. Defaults are a 0.35 m nominal tile, 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger so each module spans about 9 px; at 512 a module is about 4.5 px and edge softening takes a large share of it; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`morsetape` adds Morse-code paper tape, bringing the current catalog from 913 to 914 kinds (915 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 10 tape lines, each 64 time units wide; every line spells one word chosen by hash from ten (SOS, XYZ, CAT, PLAY, HELLO, WORLD, LIGHT, ENGINE, SIGNAL, TEXTURE) in International Morse timing: dot = 1 unit, dash = 3 units, 1 unit between marks of a letter, 3 units between letters, 3 units of blank margin at the left and blank tape for the remainder so the pattern is not cut at the tile boundary. Marks are round-ended capsules one unit thick; each line has a faint center guide, the ink has low-amplitude density variation and the paper faint fibers. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic, not a measurement of a particular telegraph tape standard: sprocket holes along the tape, ink wobble and fading are not modeled; each line holds a single word (so the 7-unit word gap never appears) and the vocabulary is a fixed ten words. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.0016 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `sandripples` adds wind-formed sand ripples, bringing the current catalog from 914 to 915 kinds (916 gallery choices including plain). A train of ripples on the integer wave vector (18, 7), about 18 crests crossing the u direction per tile; the crests are bent by two periodic low-frequency noise fields (6×6 and 24×24 cells) and the profile is asymmetric: the windward face takes 72% of the phase and rises gently, the lee face takes 28% and drops steeply, with crest and trough rounded by a smooth function. The windward side is lighter, the lee side darker with extra AO; there is also 384×384 grain relief and bright mica/mineral specks in about 5% of cells. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`frostpolygons` adds arctic patterned ground, bringing the current catalog from 915 to 916 kinds (917 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 8×8 jittered Voronoi polygons (jitter 0.7): silt polygon centers (slightly lower, mid-tone with low-frequency cloudy variation), a raised stony rim around each (darker, with round pebbles of random radius and tone 0.3–0.7), and narrow, deep, dark ice-wedge troughs (darker AO) between polygons. Polygon borders are approximated from the gap between the two nearest seed distances, not a true edge distance, so trough width varies slightly at sharp corners. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored simplified schematic, not a measurement of a particular permafrost site (such as tundra polygons or stone circles): ice-wedge profiles, freeze–thaw cycles, moss and seasonal snow are not modeled, and the rim stones vary in brightness only, with no lithology. Defaults are a 1.5 m nominal tile, 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`datamatrixcodes` adds Data Matrix 2D-code labels, bringing the current catalog from 916 to 917 kinds (918 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 3×3 ECC 200-style symbols of 18×18 modules (each with a 1-module quiet zone around it, 60×60 modules in all): the left column and bottom row form the solid L-shaped finder, the top row and right column the alternating clock track (the top row is dark on even columns and the right column is dark on even steps up from the bottom, so the top-right corner is light), and each module of the interior 16×16 data region is inked with about 50% probability from the seed. Modules are square with edges softened only against a neighbor of the other state, so runs of dark modules stay solid; the ink has low-amplitude density variation and the paper faint fibers. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the finder and clock track follow the Data Matrix structure, but the data region holds random bits, not ECC 200 codewords (no payload, Reed–Solomon error correction or codeword placement), so the symbols cannot be scanned and no scanner or decoder library was used; the tests verify only the finder, clock track, quiet zone and rough data density. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger so each module spans about 17 px (about 8.5 px at 512); 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`ecgpaper` adds ECG chart paper, bringing the current catalog from 917 to 918 kinds (919 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is 80 mm square of pink recording paper: a 1 mm minor grid and heavier lines every 5 mm (paper tone 0.96, minor lines 0.84, major lines 0.68) plus 4 ECG trace rows, each 20 mm tall with 4 heartbeats (20 mm each, about 0.8 s or 75 bpm at 25 mm/s). Every beat is a sum of Gaussian P, Q, R, S and T waves (P +0.9 mm, Q −0.8 mm, R +7 mm, S −1.8 mm, T +1.7 mm) with ±6% amplitude jitter per beat and a 0.25 mm baseline drift of one period per tile. The trace is a dark ink line with half width 0.2 mm, rendered by the first-order distance (vertical offset divided by √(1 + slope²)); at very steep spikes such as the R wave the inked line therefore grows much thicker vertically than 0.2 mm (measured: the R-wave ink reaches about 8.3 mm above baseline against the 7 mm authored amplitude). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic, not a recording or diagnostic data of any real ECG: lead labels, calibration pulses, heart-rate variability, noise, pathological waveforms and the 12-lead layout are not modeled. Defaults are a 0.08 m nominal tile (80 mm square, matching the paper's real millimetres), 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. `sheetmusic` adds sheet music, bringing the current catalog from 918 to 919 kinds (920 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 8 five-line staves (row pitch 0.125 tile, line spacing 1/64 tile), 16 beats per staff with a barline every 4 beats, and one note per beat whose pitch is hash-chosen from the 9 half-spacing positions within the staff (bottom line to top line, no ledger lines). Noteheads are tilted ellipses, about 30% hollow (half-note style) and the rest filled (quarter-note style). Stems follow the notation rule: notes below the middle line (position < 4) have stems up on the right of the head; notes on or above the middle line have stems down on the left, 3.5 spacings long. The ink has low-amplitude density variation and the paper faint fibers. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic, not any piece of music: clefs, time and key signatures, flags, beams, rests, duration-proportional spacing and lyrics are not modeled, and a hollow note does not change the beat count (every note still occupies one beat slot), so it is not playable. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.0014 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `sudokugrid` adds a Sudoku grid, bringing the current catalog from 919 to 920 kinds (921 gallery choices including plain). Each cell shows a clue digit with about 42% probability from the seed, drawn in a 3×5 pixel font (0.135 cell per pixel). The clues come from a hidden complete solution built from the canonical pattern with digit relabelling and band, in-band row and in-band column permutations, all of which preserve the Sudoku rules, so no row, column or box contains a repeated clue. The ink has low-amplitude density variation and the paper faint fibers. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the clues are a random subset of the full solution and do not guarantee a unique solution or any difficulty grade, and the font is a 3×5 pixel font rather than real print type. `measuringtape` adds a measuring tape, bringing the current catalog from 920 to 921 kinds (922 gallery choices including plain). `fretboard` adds a guitar fretboard, bringing the current catalog from 922 to 923 kinds (924 gallery choices including plain). Each tile covers one octave (from the nut to the 12th fret) of dark rosewood: fret positions follow twelve-tone equal temperament, fret n sitting at 1 − 2^(−n/12) of the scale length, normalized by the 12th fret (half the scale) onto u = 1 so it meets the next tile's nut at u = 0; each fret gap is 2^(−1/12) ≈ 0.944 of the previous one. Six strings run along u, evenly spaced across the width, with half widths growing from 0.0022 (treble side) to 0.0075 (bass side) and a faint shadow beside each; pearl dots sit at the midpoints of frets 3, 5, 7 and 9, and a symmetric double dot at the midpoint of the 12th fret. The wood grain is stretched along u. Metallic is 0 (frets and strings use brightness and roughness only, not the metal mask).

This is an authored schematic, not a measurement of a particular instrument: the scale length is normalized, so only the fret-spacing ratios exist and no real millimetre sizes; fretboard radius, neck taper, string dents and wear are not modeled, and frets and strings are not metallic reflectors (they are brighter, smoother non-metals). `crosswordgrid` adds a crossword grid, bringing the current catalog from 923 to 924 kinds (925 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one 15×15 crossword grid: about 17% of the cells are black, chosen from the seed by repeatedly adding black cells in 180°-rotationally symmetric pairs and accepting a pair only if every across and down run of white cells stays at least 3 cells long and all white cells stay connected. White cells that start an across or down word carry the standard number in reading order (1, 2, …, drawn in the cell's top-left corner in a 3×5 pixel font); the other white cells stay blank, black cells are ink-black, and thin lines separate the cells. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the cells are an empty crossword grid with no answer letters, clue text or heavy outer frame, and no word list guarantees the grid can be filled; the rules and numbering hold only inside a single tile — when the tile repeats, white runs at its edge continue across the tile boundary, so the repeated surface is not one valid large crossword. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.0014 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. The whole panel is a 12-column × 8-row grid of digits, each digit taking 4×6 dots, lit as a 3×5 pixel glyph with one unlit dot of margin to the right and below; the digit values (0–9) come from the seed. The panel carries faint grain and darker AO between discs. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`minesweeperboard` adds a Minesweeper board, bringing the current catalog from 925 to 926 kinds (927 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one 24×24 board: every cell hides a mine with 16% probability from the seed (the mines themselves are not drawn), adjacent-mine counts are computed on a torus so the tile edges join without a seam, and the board is opened by flood-fill from 7 safe zero cells (a zero cell opens all 8 neighbors). Opened cells are flat, darker and carry a thin grid line, with a digit 1–8 in a 3×5 pixel font when any neighbor is a mine; unopened cells are raised buttons with a light bevel at the top-left and a dark one at the bottom-right. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: there are no flags, question marks, exploded mines or digit colors (tones are brightness, not hue); the mines under the unopened area are fixed but invisible, so the picture only guarantees consistency of necessary conditions (see ACCEPTANCE) and not unique solvability. Because adjacency wraps at the tile boundary, this is not a standard bounded Minesweeper board. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. `tetrisstack` adds a Tetris-style stack, bringing the current catalog from 926 to 927 kinds (928 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one 16×16 well: from the seed it repeatedly tries to place one of the seven tetrominoes (I, O, T, S, Z, J, L) in a random rotation and position, accepting a placement only if it lies fully inside the well and overlaps nothing, so every piece has exactly 4 cells; each of the seven kinds has its own tone (seven brightness steps from 0.9 to 0.2), cells have bevels and a highlight, pieces are separated by dark outlines (two touching pieces of the same kind are also split by an outline) and unoccupied cells are near-black pits. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic, not a real game position: there is no gravity, line clearing, falling piece or game rule, and nothing guarantees the stack could arise in play — it is a random non-overlapping placement; the tones are brightness, not the game's standard hues. Pieces at the tile edge do not cross the boundary, so repeated tiles simply sit side by side. `hilbertcurve` adds a Hilbert curve, bringing the current catalog from 928 to 929 kinds (930 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one order-4 Hilbert space-filling curve through the centers of 16×16 = 256 cells, produced by the standard index-to-coordinate algorithm: it starts in the top-left cell and ends in the top-right cell, cells with consecutive indices are joined by line segments and no other neighboring cells are joined. The line is 0.28 cell wide with a tone ramp along the curve index from deep indigo (0.08) to gray (0.55), on paper with faint fibers and low-amplitude ink density variation. The first and last cells each extend a half-cell stub beyond the tile edge, so when the tile repeats horizontally the previous tile's end joins the next tile's start into one continuous curve; vertically adjacent tiles are not connected. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the tone jumps from lightest back to darkest at the tile seam (a tone discontinuity between index 255 and 0), which is deliberate; no marker labels the start and end, and no other order or space-filling curve is offered. `mondriancomposition` adds a Mondrian-style composition, bringing the current catalog from 929 to 930 kinds (931 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds a rectangle composition from recursive binary partitioning: the first two levels always split, after which each rectangle keeps splitting with 80% probability (at most 5 levels deep, minimum side 0.14 tile); each split line spans only the rectangle it divides, as in the paintings, with a split ratio between 35% and 65%; the tile edge also carries a black frame, so the composition is closed and continuous when repeated. Black lines have a half width of 0.0075 tile, each rectangle is filled with one of six tones (0.97 three times, 0.62, 0.4, 0.78, so about half the rectangles are white), the canvas has faint grain and the colored rectangles add brush variation. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: it is not a copy of any Mondrian work and has no red, blue and yellow — the fills are brightness only (colors interpolate linearly between the dark and light ends, so the result is grayscale); the partition rules and ratios are the author's. `lissajousgrid` adds a Lissajous-figure table, bringing the current catalog from 930 to 931 kinds (932 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds a 4×4 oscilloscope-style table of Lissajous curves: cell (column, row) draws the parametric curve x = A·sin(a·t + π/2), y = A·sin(b·t) with frequencies a = column + 1 and b = row + 1 (A = 0.4 cell, t from 0 to 2π, approximated by a 160-segment polyline), so the 16 ratios run from the 1:1 circle to 4:4; when a and b share a factor the curve retraces itself, and cases such as a = 2b degenerate into a parabola arc. Lines are bright green (half width 0.014 cell) with a soft glow on a deep-green panel, a faint cell frame and center cross graticule, and faint grain. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: oscilloscope screen curvature, phosphor trails, scan lines and readout text are not modeled, the phase is fixed at π/2 (it does not vary per cell), and the color is just a green tone interpolated linearly between the dark and light ends. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger; every sample of this material checks a 160-segment polyline, so it costs more than most materials: a one-off local Bun run sampled 512² in about 155 ms (versus about 56 ms for tumblingblocks and 17 ms for brick in the same run; not a benchmark, and neither browser nor Worker was measured); 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`zoneplates` adds Fresnel zone plates, bringing the current catalog from 931 to 932 kinds (933 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds a 2×2 array of plates with 14 zones each; the outer edge of zone k lies at radius R·√(k/N) (R = 0.42 cell, N = 14), the Fresnel zone-plate radius law (every zone has equal area); even zones (including the central disc) are open (light) and odd zones opaque (near-black), the outermost 14th zone is opaque and meets a mid-gray backing, and a light-gray retaining ring surrounds each plate. Zone edges are slightly softened and the backing and ring carry faint grain. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only the geometry of the radius law is drawn — diffraction, focus, wavelength and intensity distribution are not simulated, and the ring count and size are normalized (R and N fixed), not tied to a real design wavelength or focal length. `backgammonboard` adds a backgammon board, bringing the current catalog from 932 to 933 kinds (934 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one board: inside a frame, two halves of 6 "points" (triangles) each around a darker central bar; the 12 triangles of the top row point down and the 12 of the bottom row point up, with alternating tones along each side (0.52 and 0.34) and the two rows offset by one point; triangles are 40% of the board height long. Each side has 15 checkers (light and dark), placed at random on the 24 points with at most 5 per point and only one color per point, stacked from the board edge toward the middle, with a rim highlight and a slight rise. `jigsawpuzzle` adds a jigsaw puzzle, bringing the current catalog from 933 to 934 kinds (935 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds a 6×6-piece puzzle on a torus: every piece is based on a grid cell, and each edge between cells carries one round bulb (radius 0.115 cell, neck half width 0.05 cell, protruding 0.15 cell) whose owning side is chosen at random from the seed and which fits into the other side, so two neighboring pieces always interlock as one bulb and one socket; edges wrap at the tile boundary, so the repeated puzzle is continuous. Pieces are separated by thin cut lines with a small bevel; the picture is a low-frequency cloudy light-and-dark "image" (6×6 cells) with 48×48-cell detail, ±0.06 per-piece tone variation and grain. This is an authored schematic: the bulb is a circle on a straight neck, not the curves of a real die-cut; board thickness, printed picture content and the back of the pieces are not modeled. Piece areas differ a little because of bulbs and sockets (a piece whose bulbs and sockets cancel pairwise has plain cell area). `ramennoodles` adds ramen noodles, bringing the current catalog from 934 to 935 kinds (936 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 22 wavy noodle strands running along u, layered from top to bottom with later strands lying over earlier ones: the center line of strand i is y = (i + 0.5)/22 + 0.085·sin(2π(k·u + phase)), with k cycling through 3, 4, 5 and the phase taken from the golden ratio (the fractional part of i × 0.618…), so the strand shapes are the same for every seed and only tone and grain change with the seed; strands have a half width of 0.026 and a round tube profile (bright along the center line, darker toward the edges with lower height and ambient occlusion), ±0.06 per-strand tone variation, and about 7% of the area shows dark broth between strands. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: there are no curled noodles, breaks, oil slicks, toppings or broth reflections; because every strand is a wave with a fixed stacking order, the pile looks fairly regular. Distance to a strand uses a first-order approximation (vertical offset over √(1 + slope²)), so strand width is slightly off where the slope is steep at the crests. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.01 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger; each sample checks 22 strands, so the cost is moderate (a one-off local Bun run sampled 512² in about 200 ms, not a benchmark); 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`connectfourboard` adds a Connect Four board, bringing the current catalog from 935 to 936 kinds (937 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one 7-column × 6-row board with one extra row of base tray below: a blue panel with round holes, each hole dark (empty) or holding the first player's disc (mid tone) or the second player's disc (near-white), with an inner ring and a slightly raised rim. The position comes from simulating a legal game from the seed: the two players alternate dropping discs into random columns (the first player starts), discs stack from the bottom by gravity, and a drop that would complete four in a row is rerolled into another column; there are 18–30 moves. So every column's discs are unbroken from the bottom, the first player has either as many discs as the second or exactly one more, and nobody has completed four in a row. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: there is no real red and yellow (colors are brightness interpolated linearly between the dark and light ends, so the first player is a mid blue-gray and the second near-white); the position is a random legal one, not a played strategy, and nothing guarantees that both sides would "sensibly" have played it. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger so a hole spans about 73 px; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`bingocard` adds a bingo card, bringing the current catalog from 936 to 937 kinds (938 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is 6×6 cells; the left 5 columns × 6 rows hold one bingo card: the first row is a pale-gray "B I N G O" header (3×5 pixel font), and the five rows below hold numbers in the standard ranges — column B 1–15, I 16–30, N 31–45, G 46–60, O 61–75 — distinct within each column and chosen at random from the seed; the middle cell (third row of the N column) is the free space, marked by a gray dot; about 25% of the numbered cells carry a daub circle. The card has a heavier outer frame; the sixth column on the right is blank margin so repeated cards are separated. Metallic and mortar are 0.

The position comes from the seed by starting at the solved end state (one peg in the center) and playing 8 random moves backwards (each reverse jump turns "peg, empty, empty" in a line into "empty, peg, peg"), so the picture — 9 pegs, or fewer if the attempt budget runs out — can always be solved to a single peg by playing the jumps forward. `xylophonebars` adds xylophone bars, bringing the current catalog from 938 to 939 kinds (940 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 12 wooden bars side by side (the twelve semitones of an octave), all centered on the middle line of the tile; the first is the longest (0.9 tile) and each following bar is 2^(−1/24) ≈ 0.9715 of the previous one — a tuned bar's frequency goes as 1/length², so one equal-tempered semitone (frequency ratio 2^(1/12)) shortens it by 2^(−1/24), and twelve semitones (an octave) by 2^(−1/2). Each bar has a suspension hole 22.4% in from each end (the node positions of the first free–free bending mode), and the holes of neighboring bars are joined by a thin line (the cord); the wood grain runs along the bar and the bar tone lightens slightly from long to short on a dark felt background. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only the length ratios and node positions are drawn — bar thickness, width and cross-section (real xylophone bars are often undercut to tune the overtones) are not modeled, nor are resonator tubes; the cord is a straight line between holes and snaps back at the tile seam (from the last bar to the next tile's first bar), a deliberate discontinuity. `sliderulescale` adds slide-rule scales, bringing the current catalog from 939 to 940 kinds (941 gallery choices including plain). Each tile stacks 8 ivory logarithmic C scales, one decade spanning the whole tile width: the graduation x is drawn at u = log10(x), so 10 coincides with the 1 of the next tile and the tile repeats seamlessly. Graduations follow the usual rule — every 0.02 in [1, 2), every 0.05 in [2, 4), every 0.1 in [4, 10) — for 150 ticks at three lengths: integers (9, longest), tenths in [1, 4) and halves in [4, 10) (33 medium) and the remaining 108 shortest; each integer tick has a 3×5 dot-matrix digit 1 to 9 to its right. Each scale has a thin line along its top and bottom, the ink varies slightly in density and the paper has a fine grain. Metallic and mortar are 0.

Each tile draws one hypotrochoid per quadrant (the curve traced by a pen at some distance from the center of a small gear rolling inside a large ring) with ring/gear radius ratios 5/3, 8/3, 7/2 and 9/4, giving 5, 8, 7 and 9 lobes (for coprime R and r the lobe count equals R); the curve closes after t has run through 2π·r/gcd(R, r). The pen distance varies with the seed and quadrant between 0.37 and 0.73 gear radii and each figure is rotated by the seed; the pen always reaches exactly the outer circle (radius 0.215 tile), so all lobe tips lie on one circle. The four quadrants use slightly different ink brightness and the paper has a fine grain. Metallic and mortar are 0.

Implementation: when the sampler is created the curves are stamped (about 108 thousand points) into a 640×640 Float32 ink-coverage mask (about 1.6 MB, one per sampler) and every sample is just a bilinear lookup; the mask resolution is fixed at 640, so above 640 px the lines are magnified by the bilinear filter and get slightly softer rather than sharper.

This is an authored schematic: only four fixed ring/gear ratios are drawn (not arbitrary R, r), the curve is a polyline of uniformly spaced t samples (9000 points per loop, not an exact distance field); colors are brightness interpolation (near-black ink on cream paper) and do not represent pen hues. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `juliacells` adds Julia-set cells, bringing the current catalog from 941 to 942 kinds (943 gallery choices including plain). Each tile draws one filled Julia set z → z² + c per quadrant with a real c (about −0.4, −0.75, −1.0 and −1.25, each jittered by up to ±0.04 by the seed; for real c in [−2, 1/4] the set is connected and the picture is mirror symmetric in both axes). Each cell's view radius is 2, equal to the escape radius, so points on a cell border escape immediately and there is no seam between cells or at the tile repeat. The interior (points still bounded after 96 iterations) is near black; outside, the smooth escape count μ = n + 1 − log₂(ln|z| / ln 2) drives a glow 1 − exp(−μ/9) from dark to bright, and height and roughness follow the same glow. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only four real-parameter Julia sets — no Mandelbrot set and no complex c (a complex c is not mirror symmetric and would leave a seam at the tile border); the iteration cap is 96, so slowly escaping points near the boundary are drawn as interior; colors are brightness interpolation (near-black navy to warm cream) and do not represent any particular palette. `weavingdraft` adds a weaving draft, bringing the current catalog from 944 to 945 kinds (946 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a 16×16-cell sheet showing the full draft for a four-shaft loom: the 12×4 block at the top left is the threading (which shaft each warp thread runs through, one mark per column, shaft 1 in the row nearest the drawdown), the 4×4 block at the top right is the tie-up (which shafts each treadle lifts), the 12×4 block at the bottom right is the treadling (which treadle is pressed for each weft pass, one mark per row), and the 12×12 block at the bottom left is the drawdown they determine: a dark cell means that warp thread floats on top for that pass (its shaft is lifted), a light cell means the weft is on top. Threading and treadling are chosen at random by the seed, and every treadle lifts a non-empty, non-full set of shafts (1 to 3), so the drawdown is fully fixed by the rule. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`knightstour` adds a knight's tour, bringing the current catalog from 946 to 947 kinds (948 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is an 8×8 chessboard of alternating light and dark squares, every square numbered 1 to 64 in 3×5 dot-matrix digits along an open knight's tour (each step an L-shaped knight move, no square visited twice), with a faint thin line joining the centers of consecutively numbered squares. The tour is found when the sampler is created by depth-first search that tries the square with the fewest onward moves first (Warnsdorff's rule), breaking ties by the seed; each attempt has a node budget (40000) and a failure restarts from another square (up to 60 attempts); the start and the route vary with the seed. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only an open route is drawn, not required to return to the start (not a closed tour); there are no pieces; where the thin line crosses digits the digits are drawn on top of it; the search is a budgeted heuristic, not exhaustive — on 600 seeds a complete 64-step route was in fact found every time (the slowest creation was about 49 ms, a one-off local measurement and not a benchmark), but that does not prove every seed succeeds; if all 60 attempts failed, the squares reached would be numbered and the rest left blank (not observed here). Colors are brightness interpolation (light/dark cream squares and near-black ink) and do not represent a real board material. `graycodediscs` adds Gray-code encoder discs, bringing the current catalog from 947 to 948 kinds (949 gallery choices including plain). The rim carries thin sector tick marks, there is a dark shaft hole in the center and a mid-grey mat outside the disc. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`code39barcodes` adds Code 39 barcodes, bringing the current catalog from 948 to 949 kinds (950 gallery choices including plain). Each tile has 6 rows of barcodes, each of the form `*XXXXX*`: the start/stop character `*` around 5 characters chosen by the seed (0–9, A–Z, `-`, `.`). Every character is 9 elements (5 black bars and 4 spaces, starting with a bar) of which exactly 3 are wide (3× the narrow width) and 6 narrow; characters are separated by one narrow space, with quiet zones of at least 10 narrow units before and after. The paper is cream, the bars carry slight ink density variation and grain. Metallic and mortar are 0.

The pattern table was typed from memory and decoded back independently in the tests using the structural rule described on Wikipedia's Code 39 page (two wide bars encode a number 1–10 with the weights 1, 2, 4, 7, 0; the one wide space out of four picks one of the groups U–Z plus symbols / digits / A–J / K–T), confirming that the patterns of all 38 data characters and of the `*` delimiter follow that rule; they were not checked against a real barcode scanner or the full text of ISO/IEC 16388, and the codes were never actually scanned.

This is an authored schematic: no Code 39 check digit (the symbology does not require one), none of the symbols `$`, `/`, `+`, `%` and the space character (it can be encoded but this alphabet does not use it), no human-readable text; the wide-to-narrow ratio is fixed at 3:1 and a unit is 1/132 of the tile, so very low resolutions (such as 32) cannot resolve the narrow bars. `quasicrystalwaves` adds quasicrystal-style waves, bringing the current catalog from 953 to 954 kinds (955 gallery choices including plain). Five plane waves cos(2π(m·x) + φ) are summed, with integer wave vectors m = (6, 0), (2, 6), (−5, 4), (−5, −4), (2, −6) that point roughly in the five directions of a regular pentagon (neighboring angles within 10° of 72°, length ratio below 1.15) and phases φ chosen by the seed; the sum S goes through the monotonic map 0.5 + 0.5·tanh(0.7·S) to the brightness (height and roughness come from the same sum), giving an approximately five-fold symmetric picture of spots and pentagram-like structures. Because the wave vectors are integers the whole pattern is exactly periodic over the tile and repeats seamlessly. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`chesterfieldtufting` adds Chesterfield diamond-tufted leather, bringing the current catalog from 956 to 957 kinds (958 gallery choices including plain). Each tile has a round button at each of the 8 grid points of a 4×4 grid whose index sum is even, with dark creases pulled diagonally between neighboring buttons and each diamond between the creases puffed up into a cushion. In the rotated coordinates s = 4(u + v), t = 4(u − v) the buttons sit at even integers and the creases are the lines s = 2m and t = 2m; inside a diamond the height is (sin(πs/2)·sin(πt/2))^0.7, highest at the middle and 0 on the creases. The brightness rises with the height from near-black at the creases to warm leather brown, the hide has small wrinkles and grain, and the buttons are small brighter discs with a rim. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only the diamond tufting pattern — no button holes or stitches and no finer wrinkles radiating from the buttons; the creases are perfectly straight between buttons; the leather texture is brightness noise, not real pores; colors are brightness interpolation (near-black brown to brick brown) and do not represent a particular leather. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.02 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement, a strong relief) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. `sundialplate` adds a sundial plate, bringing the current catalog from 959 to 960 kinds (961 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds the face of a horizontal sundial (a bronze disc of radius 0.475 tile on a dark brown mat): a small hub at the center where the gnomon would stand and 13 hour lines fanning out over the upper half, the noon line vertical and heavier, the line h hours from noon making the angle atan(sin φ · tan(15°·h)) with it for h = −6 to 6 (the ±6 hour lines are horizontal), where φ is the latitude, chosen by the seed between 25° and 55°. There are three concentric rings (radius 0.2, 0.3 and 0.385 tile) and the hour numerals (6, 7, …, 11, 12, 1, …, 6 in 3×5 dot matrix) beyond the end of each line; the numerals of neighboring hours alternate between two radii so that the ones near noon do not overlap at low latitudes. `doubleslitfringes` adds double-slit interference fringes, bringing the current catalog from 960 to 961 kinds (962 gallery choices including plain). Each tile stacks four far-field double-slit patterns whose intensity along the horizontal is I(x) = cos²(πx/p) · sinc²(πx/(r·p)), with x the offset from the center, p = 1/16 tile the fringe period and r the slit separation divided by the slit width; the four panels use r = 2, 3, 4, 5: the fringes sit at whole multiples of p, and when the order m is a multiple of r it falls exactly on a zero of the single-slit sinc² envelope and is missing. The brightness is I^0.6, on a dark background with cream fringes and a thin dark gap between panels. The pattern is mirror symmetric about the center, so it is continuous at the tile seam and repeats seamlessly. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: it is the idealized far-field (Fraunhofer) formula, not an experimental image — no finite screen distance, finite source width or non-monochromatic blurring of the fringes, and no physical intensity units; the pattern is one-dimensional along the horizontal and merely repeated vertically; the seed only changes a very fine grain; colors are brightness (near-black blue to cream) and do not represent a particular wavelength of light. `fibonaccisquares` adds Fibonacci squares with a golden spiral, bringing the current catalog from 961 to 962 kinds (963 gallery choices including plain). In the middle of each tile is a 13 × 21 unit rectangle (unit = 1/24 tile) tiled by seven squares of side 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 13 (aspect ratio 21/13 ≈ 1.615, close to the golden ratio; the areas 1 + 1 + 4 + 9 + 25 + 64 + 169 = 273 = 13 × 21 fill it exactly); each square is attached to one side of the current rectangle in the order right, top, left, bottom and has its own brightness; inside every square a quarter circle of radius equal to its side is centered on one of its corners, and neighboring arcs are tangent at their shared end point, forming one continuous golden spiral. Around the rectangle is cream paper. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the spiral is the Fibonacci-square approximation (quarter-circle arcs joined tangentially, with curvature jumping at the joints), not a true logarithmic spiral; the rectangle does not fill the tile and leaves blank margins, so there are gaps between the figures when the tile repeats; only seven squares (the largest 13) are drawn and it cannot be extended; the seed only changes the paper grain. `bluenoisemask` adds a blue-noise mask, bringing the current catalog from 962 to 963 kinds (964 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a 64×64 blue-noise dither mask built with the void-and-cluster algorithm (Ulichney): on a torus (edges wrapping) a Gaussian energy (σ = 1.5) finds the "tightest cluster" and the "largest void"; about 10% random initial points are relaxed to a stable pattern, then all 4096 texels are ranked 0 to 4095 with every rank used exactly once; brightness = rank ÷ 4095, so the brightness histogram is exactly flat and low-frequency energy is strongly suppressed. The mask is computed on a torus and repeats seamlessly; height rises with brightness and roughness rises slightly. Metallic and mortar are 0.

One-off local measurement (seed 0, discrete Fourier power of the 64×64 mask divided by the power expected for white noise): about 0.000 for frequencies of radius 1 to 5, about 0.003 for radius 8 to 12 and about 1.61 for radius 24 to 31 (near Nyquist); a random permutation of the same variance (white noise) gives about 1.21, 1.14 and 0.96. Creating a sampler takes about 66 ms (one-off, not a benchmark).

This is an authored product with limits: the mask size is fixed at 64×64 texels (larger would make the algorithm too slow) and it is sampled nearest-neighbour, so on a 512 px image each texel is an 8×8 px block (for texel-exact blue noise set the size to 64 or sample it with repeat in a shader); the seed only chooses the initial random points — different seeds give different masks of similar spectral quality; colors are brightness with no hue meaning. Defaults are a 0.2 m nominal tile, 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. No three-backend or cross-browser verification is claimed.

`elementaryautomata` adds one-dimensional elementary cellular automata, bringing the current catalog from 963 to 964 kinds (965 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is 2×2 panels of 31×31 cells, each evolving one Wolfram rule from top to bottom — rule 90 top left (Sierpinski triangle), 110 top right, 150 bottom left and 184 bottom right (the traffic rule): row 0 is the middle cell plus a sparse seed-chosen scatter of about 12%, and each next row is computed from the previous one by the rule (on a ring of 31 cells, the ends wrapping). Live cells are small near-black squares, dead cells small light-grey squares, a thin line separates the panels and the paper is cream. Because the ring has 31 cells (odd), rule 90 does not die out to all zeros after a few steps the way it does with 32 cells; the pattern continues to the bottom. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only four rules, a fixed width of 31 cells and 31 rows; the ring boundary makes the pattern wrap around the left and right edges (it does not continue into the neighboring panels); the first row contains random points, so it is not the classic single-seed triangle (set seedDensity to 0 for a single seed); "an odd ring does not die out" was observed on the seeds tested here and has no mathematical proof; colors are brightness (near-black ink, light-grey grid, cream paper). Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.0014 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. `mastermindboard` adds a Mastermind board, bringing the current catalog from 964 to 965 kinds (966 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a 6-column × 9-row board: the top row is the revealed secret code (4 pegs chosen at random from 6 colors) and each of the 8 rows below is a random guess of 4 pegs; to the right of each guess are two columns forming a 2×2 block of feedback holes scored by the rules — a "exact" peg (right color in the right place, bright, 0.98) is placed first, then a "partial" peg (right color in the wrong place, near-black, 0.04), and the remaining holes stay empty — filled left to right, top to bottom. The 6 peg colors are six brightnesses (0.34 to 0.9, 0.12 apart), the holes are dark brown and the board is wood brown with a grain stretched vertically; a line separates the code row from the guesses. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the guesses are random, not reasoned from earlier feedback (so later guesses need not agree with earlier feedback, and no row is guaranteed to be a complete hit); there is no cover hiding the code; colors are only brightness and the six peg colors are hard to tell apart at small sizes; the feedback pegs' conventional "black/white" for exact/partial is shown here as bright/dark. `magicsquares` adds magic squares, bringing the current catalog from 966 to 967 kinds (968 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one magic square per quadrant: order 3 (Lo Shu), order 4 (Dürer's square), and orders 5 and 7 (the odd orders by the Siamese method: start in the middle of the top row, move up and right, and step down one row when the cell is taken); each square is rotated 0 to 3 times by the seed and possibly reflected (rotation and reflection keep the property). So the numbers of each square are exactly 1 to n² once each, and every row, column and both diagonals sum to the magic constant n(n²+1)/2 (15, 34, 65, 175). Numbers are 3×5 dot matrix (one or two digits) with grid lines and a heavier outer frame on cream paper. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the numbers of the Lo Shu and Dürer squares were typed from memory and verified by the condition "every row, column and diagonal sums to the constant and the numbers are 1 to n²" (other properties of Dürer's square, such as the four corners and the central 2×2 also summing to 34, are not tested); the order-5 and order-7 squares come from the algorithm and are not particular traditional squares; there is no order-6 or other even order (they need different constructions); the order-7 cells are small (about 0.07 tile — about 36 px at 512, and a two-digit dot-matrix pixel is only about 4 px). Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.0014 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `oghaminscription` adds an Ogham inscription, bringing the current catalog from 969 to 970 kinds (971 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a rough grey stone face (fine-grained and coarse brightness variation) carved with eight horizontal rows of Ogham: each row has a horizontal stem line and a word is written left to right as letters of one to five short strokes. The four aicmi (groups) are drawn differently: group 1 (B L F S N) hangs below the stem, group 2 (H D T C Q) rises above it, group 3 (M G NG Z R) crosses the stem diagonally and group 4 (A O U E I, the vowels) is short notches on the stem; the number of strokes (1 to 5) picks the letter within the group. `gameoflife` adds Conway's Game of Life, bringing the current catalog from 970 to 971 kinds (972 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is split into 2×2 cell boards of 20×20 which, in reading order (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), are four consecutive generations of Conway's Game of Life: the seed makes a random initial state of density 0.36, runs it for 10 generations on a torus (edges wrap), and four consecutive generations by the rule — a live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbours survives, a dead cell with exactly 3 is born — fill the quadrants, so each board is the next generation of the one before. Live cells are bright green squares, dead cells dark green, with lighter grid lines and frames on a near-black background. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the start is a random soup, not a particular pattern (no gliders or other structures are placed on purpose); the boards are only 20×20 (torus); the burn-in is 10 generations instead of a longer one because with 24 generations as few as 21 live cells were left among 14 seeds (with my first one-dimensional hash for the soup even seed 0 was left with 8, and large empty areas appeared, so a two-dimensional hash is used), whereas 10 generations gives 59 to 121 live cells out of 400; the opposite edges of each board connect on the torus, but this wrap is not drawn on the tile. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `pascalmodulo` adds Pascal's triangle modulo n, bringing the current catalog from 971 to 972 kinds (973 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is split into 2×2 left-aligned 32-row Pascal triangles: the c-th square of row r follows the recurrence (each cell is the sum of the two cells above it) reduced modulo 2, 3, 4 and 5, one modulus per quadrant, with the seed choosing which modulus goes in which quadrant. A larger residue is a brighter square (brightness evenly spread between 0.2 and 0.94), the area above the diagonal is dark empty background, and each board has a thin frame. This is an authored schematic: only 32 rows are shown; residues are brightness, not hue (the five levels for modulo 5 are about 0.185 apart and are hard to tell apart at small sizes); residue 0 is not "empty" but a darker square (brightness 0.2) — empty is only above the diagonal; each of the four moduli appears once. `dragoncurve` adds a dragon curve, bringing the current catalog from 972 to 973 kinds (974 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is an order-11 Heighway dragon curve (the curve obtained by folding a strip of paper in half 11 times and unfolding it): 2048 unit-length lattice segments whose turn sequence is the regular paper-folding sequence (each round keeps the earlier turns, adds one left turn, then the earlier turns reversed and swapped). The curve is drawn as a thin line along the lattice with square joints at the corners and a brightness gradient along the path from dim orange to bright orange (0.42 at the start, 0.96 at the end) on a near-black deep purple background. The curve's rotation (0 to 3 quarter turns) and whether it is mirrored are set by the seed, and the whole curve is scaled to fit and centred in the tile with a margin. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: there is a single dragon curve whose shape does not vary with the seed (only its orientation and mirroring); it occupies the middle of the tile with flat background around it and does not fill the tile; the line width is about 0.34 of the lattice spacing, which at order 11 is about 0.02 tile — only about 3.5 px wide at 512 px; the order-11 curve's segments never overlap but do meet at vertices (so the joint squares can look like crossings). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `cantordust` adds Cantor dust, bringing the current catalog from 973 to 974 kinds (975 gallery choices including plain). The bottom half is three steps of Cantor dust: a 27×27 grid in which only the cells whose column and row indices both have no base-3 digit 1 (8×8 = 64) are lit, on a lighter square base. The background is dark blue-black with faint grain. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the Cantor set stops at step 5 (243 cells, each about 4 px wide at 1024 px) and the dust at 3 steps (27×27) — the real Cantor set is the limit of infinitely many steps; the middle third is always removed (I first let the seed choose which digit to remove, but removing digit 2 pushed all of the dust into a corner where it was hard to see, so it is fixed to 1), and the seed changes only the grain; it is not a visual proof about the fractal. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. `mayansums` adds Maya addition, bringing the current catalog from 977 to 978 kinds (979 gallery choices including plain). In each of the four quadrants of the tile a sum a + b = c is carved on a rough grey stone, with the numbers in Maya base-20 notation: each number is two stacked cells (the upper one the 20s digit, the lower one the units digit, each 0 to 19), and inside a cell 0 is an elliptical shell ring, 1 to 4 is a row of dots, 5 is a bar, and 6 to 19 is some bars (each worth 5) stacked at the bottom with a row of dots (each worth 1) above them. The seed picks a and b between 10 and 199 and c = a + b (at most 398, still a two-digit base-20 number); a plus and an equals sign are carved between the three columns. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the numerals are a simplified drawing of Maya base-20 digits (bars, dots, shell zero), not researched glyph forms, and the 18-based position of the Long Count calendar (where the second place only goes to 17) is not used; the sums are drawn only from the range 10 to 199 and the upper 20s cell can be 0 (a shell); the carving is just a recess darker than the stone, without weathering or chipping. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.006 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`sortingnetworks` adds sorting network diagrams, bringing the current catalog from 978 to 979 kinds (980 gallery choices including plain). In each of the four quadrants of the tile an 8-wire sorting network is drawn: eight horizontal wires (0 to 7 from top to bottom) and each comparator is a bright vertical bar with a dot at each end joining the two wires it compares (the smaller value goes to the upper wire). The seed picks one of two networks per quadrant: Batcher's odd-even merge sort (19 comparators) or the bitonic sorter (24 comparators, in its all-ascending form); every comparator gets its own column, left to right in execution order. A dark blue panel with faint grain and a thin frame. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only 8 wires and two networks; to keep nested comparators from overlapping, each comparator has a column to itself (so the comparators of one layer are not drawn in a shared column as in the standard layered drawing); the test reads the comparator network back and checks with the 0-1 principle that it sorts all 256 binary inputs, but does not show that it has the fewest possible comparators. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`primesieve` adds a prime sieve, bringing the current catalog from 979 to 980 kinds (981 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a 16×16 board of rounded squares holding 256 consecutive integers row by row, left to right and top to bottom, starting at a number the seed picks between 1 and 745. Primes are the brightest yellow squares and are raised; composites are shaded by their smallest prime factor into five grey-yellow levels (dark to bright) for 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 or more; the number 1 (if the window contains it) is the darkest square. The primes therefore sit exactly where the sieve of Eratosthenes leaves gaps, and multiples of 2 show up as dark vertical stripes every other column. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: there are no digits on the tile, so the numbers can only be inferred from the pattern; the smallest prime factors of 11 or more share one level (11, 13, 17… are not separated); the largest start is 745, so the window goes up to 1000 (the largest smallest prime factor is 31); brightness is grayscale, not hue; primality is decided by trial division, not by implementing the sieve. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`knockoutbracket` adds a knockout tournament bracket, bringing the current catalog from 980 to 981 kinds (982 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is the tree of a 16-team single-elimination tournament: on the left, round one is teams 1 to 16 shuffled by the seed (dot-matrix numbers, two glyphs for two digits), and to the right come the quarter-finals, semi-finals, final and champion as five columns of boxes, with the two boxes of each match joined by lines into the next column, whose box holds the winner of that match (the seed randomly picks the upper or the lower team), so every winner's number equals one of the two boxes that feed it, and the rightmost, brighter box is the champion. Light boxes, dark numbers and grey connectors on a dark blue background. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the results are entirely random and do not represent strength or a score; there are no scores, team names or dates; it is fixed at 16 teams with no byes or third-place match; the numbers are 3×5 dot matrix and a two-digit number is about 0.05 tile wide. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`skyscraperpuzzles` adds Skyscraper puzzles, bringing the current catalog from 981 to 982 kinds (983 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is split into 2×2 solved Skyscraper puzzles of order 4, 5, 6 and 7 in reading order: the middle is an n×n grid in which each cell is the height of a building (a dot-matrix digit from 1 to n, with a slightly darker and higher base for taller buildings) and every row and column holds 1 to n once each; the ring around it holds the clues giving how many buildings can be seen looking in from that side (taller buildings hide shorter ones behind them, so only buildings taller than all before them are counted). The digits are 3×5 dot matrix on cream paper with thin grid lines and a frame. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the tile shows the solved answer with all four sides of clues (a real puzzle gives only the clues and hides the digits inside); the solutions are cyclic Latin squares with row, column and symbol permutations, so they do not cover all possible solutions; the digits 1 to n are printed in dot matrix and the order-7 cells are small (about 0.05 tile). Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`pianoroll` adds a piano roll, bringing the current catalog from 982 to 983 kinds (984 gallery choices including plain). Each tile looks like a piano-roll editor: on the left a keyboard strip of 24 semitones (two octaves) with white keys as bright rows and black keys (C♯, D♯, F♯, G♯ and A♯ of each octave) as dark rows, and on the right a grid of 24 rows × 32 steps (with a more visible beat line every 4 steps) in which a melody is drawn as bright blue bars. The melody uses a major scale picked by the seed (one of the 12 tonics), starts on the tonic, moves one or two scale degrees at a time without repeating a pitch, with notes of 1 to 4 steps until the 32 steps are full; higher notes are brighter. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the melody is a random walk with no rhythmic or harmonic musicality; the pitch range is fixed at 24 semitones (two octaves) with the tonic in the middle-to-upper part; only a major scale is used, with no modulation, chords or rests; the keyboard strip is drawn as bright and dark rows, not as real key shapes. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`binaryclock` adds a binary clock, bringing the current catalog from 983 to 984 kinds (985 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is split into 2×2 clock panels that show four consecutive seconds in reading order: the clock shows hh:mm:ss as six decimal digits in binary coded decimal (BCD), each digit a column of four dots whose bits from top to bottom are 8, 4, 2 and 1, bright green meaning 1 and dark meaning 0. The start time is picked by the seed anywhere in a day (00:00:00 to 23:59:59), so the last column (the units of the seconds) advances from panel to panel, and when the seconds roll over (for example at 59) the carry runs on into the minutes and hours, wrapping from 23:59:59 to 00:00:00. A thin frame surrounds each dark panel. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: it is a 24-hour clock only, with no date or milliseconds; the start time comes from the seed and the nine seeds in the tests do not necessarily include a minute or day rollover (the modulo logic for the carry is written but not covered by these seeds — see ACCEPTANCE); the dots carry no labels for their bit weights (8, 4, 2, 1). Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`to92packagefaces` adds four rotated/jittered 2×2 TO-92 front schematics, bringing the current catalog from 885 to 886 kinds (887 gallery choices including plain). Matte-black D-shaped bodies have straight sides, flat bottoms and upper elliptical domes; three equally spaced parallel straight neutral-metal leads have broad root shoulders and narrow tails, with roots masked by the body. No exposed tab, mounting hole or markings are drawn. Full leads have M1; body/backing have M0, with C1 boundary blends. Authored normalized heights are backing .02 < lead .44 < body .68.

The dimension reference is the actually downloaded and raster-viewed [onsemi P2N2222A/D, January 2013 Rev. 7, PDF page 6](https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/p2n2222a-d.pdf#page=6): embedded drawing 98ASB42022B, TO-92 (TO-226), CASE 29-11, Issue AM, dated 09 MAR 2007, drawing page 1 of 2, STRAIGHT LEAD BULK PACK view. Its A 4.45–5.20 mm, B 4.32–5.33 mm, G 1.15–1.39 mm and K ≥12.70 mm are dimension references only, not measurements of the artwork. The upper half ellipse, proportions, shoulders, color, roughness, AO and heights are authored simplifications, not exact CAD. No chemistry, plating, optical or electrical properties are inferred; no source artwork is shipped.

`ftypefemalefaces` adds four 2×2 bare F-type female bulkhead front schematics, bringing the catalog from 883 to 884 kinds: six-flat nickel-plated metal hex bases, concentric raised round shoulders, CLOSED unkeyed raised circular lips, pale P.P. dielectric disks and tiny deeper dark opaque central female entries.
